input.prompt: An authentic Srikalahasti kalamkari hand-painted cotton roundel, photographed flat and straight-on. Match the attached reference cloth exactly in palette, kalam line quality, dotted and cross-hatched fill patterns, cotton weave texture and lotus motifs. Composition: one single large circular medallion centred on a plain flat square of undyed ecru cotton; the medallion fills about 88 percent of the frame width, with only a thin margin of plain ecru cloth around it. The medallion's outer ring is a border of pointed lotus petals drawn in kalam outline with dotted madder-red fills, between two thin rings of dotted pattern. Inside the ring the ground is dyed deep madder red. At the exact centre sits one open lotus flower in ecru with red dot fills and green leaves. Arranged evenly around the central lotus, each object clearly separated and drawn large enough to read: (1) a single long painter's brush lying diagonally with a pointed tip, beside a small row of three round clay dye pots filled with indigo, turmeric yellow and red dye; (2) a pair of South Indian dancer's ankle bells, gajjelu: two rows of many small round brass-yellow bells strung on a padded band with tasselled cords, drawn in flat turmeric yellow with black outline; (3) a doctor's stethoscope drawn as a smooth looping indigo tube with a round chest-piece and two earpieces, curving gracefully like a vine. Small lotus buds, paisley leaves and dotted vine tendrils fill the gaps between the objects. Style: freehand kalam (bamboo pen) outlines in iron-black with confident, slightly irregular line weight; flat natural vegetable-dye fills only: deep madder red, indigo blue, myrobalan-turmeric yellow, green made from indigo over yellow, and undyed ecru cotton; dense hand-drawn fill patterns of dots, cross-hatching, scales and tiny petals; visible hand-woven cotton weave and slight dye bleed. Completely flat, no perspective, no shading, no gradients, no metallic gold, no 3D, no photorealism. No people, no hands, no faces. No text, no letters, no writing, no numbers, no symbols, no lamps, no diyas, no candles, no fire, no flames.
